LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file defines metadata for the `linux-cjktty-headers` package, which is a kernel build with additional patches applied (specifically cjktty-patches for CJK font support in TTY). The sources are fetched from trusted and well-known locations: the main Linux kernel tarball comes from kernel.org (via CDN), Arch Linux's own patched diff is downloaded from GitHub releases, and two patches are pulled from a GitHub repository maintained by user `bigshans`. All PGP keys used for verification are explicitly listed, including those of the Arch Linux kernel team.

Checksums are provided via both SHA-256 and BLAKE2 (b2sums), with `SKIP` only used for signature files — a standard practice since detached signatures are verified using GPG, not hash sums. The use of `config::https://...` to fetch the kernel configuration is normal in Arch packaging. No scripts or executable logic are present in this file; it only declares sources and integrity checks. There is no evidence of obfuscated downloads, unauthorized network access, or data exfiltration mechanisms.

Although one patch source (`https://github.com/bigshans/cjktty-patches/`) is hosted outside official Arch infrastructure, it is directly related to the package’s purpose (adding CJK TTY support), and such third-party patches are common in customized kernel builds. The inclusion of these patches does not constitute a supply-chain attack unless they were being silently injected or hidden — here, they are fully declared and checksummed.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious content; standard kernel packaging with declared patches
</summary>
</security_assessment>
